import Mathlib

structure BipartiteGraph where
  adj : Array (Array Nat)

def BipartiteGraph.well_formed (g : BipartiteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.adj.size →
    ∀ v, v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → v < g.adj.size

def BipartiteGraph.size (g : BipartiteGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def BipartiteGraph.has_edge (g : BipartiteGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  u < g.adj.size ∧
  v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[]

def BipartiteGraph.is_valid_coloring (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : Array Bool) : Prop :=
  colors.size = g.size ∧
  ∀ u v, g.has_edge u v →
    u < colors.size → v < colors.size → colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false

def BipartiteGraph.is_bipartite (g : BipartiteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ colors, g.is_valid_coloring colors

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def check_bipartite_precond (graph : BipartiteGraph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def allColorings : Nat → List (List Bool)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n + 1 =>
      (allColorings n).map (false :: ·) ++
      (allColorings n).map (true :: ·)

def neighborsColoringOK
    (colors : List Bool) (u : Nat) : List Nat → Bool
  | [] => true
  | v :: vs =>
      decide (colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false) &&
        neighborsColoringOK colors u vs

def verticesColoringOK
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool) : List Nat → Bool
  | [] => true
  | u :: us =>
      neighborsColoringOK colors u (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList &&
        verticesColoringOK g colors us

def coloringOK (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool) : Bool :=
  decide (colors.length = g.size) &&
    verticesColoringOK g colors (List.range g.size)

def searchColorings (g : BipartiteGraph) :
    List (List Bool) → Option (List Bool)
  | [] => none
  | colors :: rest =>
      if coloringOK g colors then
        some colors
      else
        searchColorings g rest
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def check_bipartite (graph : BipartiteGraph)
    (h_precond : check_bipartite_precond graph) : Option (Array Bool) :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match searchColorings graph (allColorings graph.size) with
  | some colors => some colors.toArray
  | none => none
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def check_bipartite_postcond (graph : BipartiteGraph) (result : Option (Array Bool))
    (_ : check_bipartite_precond graph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  match result with
  | some colors => graph.is_valid_coloring colors
  | none => ¬ graph.is_bipartite
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem mem_allColorings_iff (colors : List Bool) (n : Nat) :
    colors ∈ allColorings n ↔ colors.length = n := by
  induction n generalizing colors with
  | zero =>
      cases colors <;> simp [allColorings]
  | succ n ih =>
      cases colors with
      | nil =>
          simp [allColorings]
      | cons color rest =>
          cases color <;> simp [allColorings, ih]

theorem neighborsColoringOK_eq_true_iff
    (colors : List Bool) (u : Nat) (neighbors : List Nat) :
    neighborsColoringOK colors u neighbors = true ↔
      ∀ v ∈ neighbors,
        colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false := by
  induction neighbors with
  | nil =>
      simp [neighborsColoringOK]
  | cons v vs ih =>
      simp [neighborsColoringOK, ih]

theorem verticesColoringOK_eq_true_iff
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool) (vertices : List Nat) :
    verticesColoringOK g colors vertices = true ↔
      ∀ u ∈ vertices,
        ∀ v ∈ (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList,
          colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false := by
  induction vertices with
  | nil =>
      simp [verticesColoringOK]
  | cons u us ih =>
      simp only [verticesColoringOK, Bool.and_eq_true,
        neighborsColoringOK_eq_true_iff, ih, List.mem_cons]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hu, hus⟩ x hx
        rcases hx with rfl | hx
        · exact hu
        · exact hus x hx
      · intro h
        constructor
        · exact h u (by simp)
        · intro x hx
          exact h x (by simp [hx])

theorem coloringOK_eq_true_iff (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool) :
    coloringOK g colors = true ↔
      colors.length = g.size ∧
      ∀ u ∈ List.range g.size,
        ∀ v ∈ (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList,
          colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false := by
  simp only [coloringOK, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
    verticesColoringOK_eq_true_iff]

theorem searchColorings_some_ok
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (c : List Bool) (cs : List (List Bool))
    (h : searchColorings g cs = some c) :
    coloringOK g c = true := by
  induction cs with
  | nil =>
      simp [searchColorings] at h
  | cons a cs ih =>
      cases ha : coloringOK g a with
      | false =>
          simp [searchColorings, ha] at h
          exact ih h
      | true =>
          simp [searchColorings, ha] at h
          subst c
          exact ha

theorem searchColorings_none_iff
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (cs : List (List Bool)) :
    searchColorings g cs = none ↔
      ∀ c, c ∈ cs → coloringOK g c = false := by
  induction cs with
  | nil =>
      simp [searchColorings]
  | cons a cs ih =>
      cases ha : coloringOK g a <;>
        simp [searchColorings, ha, ih]

theorem coloringOK_sound
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool)
    (h : coloringOK g colors = true) :
    g.is_valid_coloring colors.toArray := by
  rw [coloringOK_eq_true_iff] at h
  rcases h with ⟨hsize, hedges⟩
  constructor
  · simpa [BipartiteGraph.size] using hsize
  · intro u v huv _hu _hv
    have huRange : u ∈ List.range g.size := by
      exact List.mem_range.mpr huv.1
    have hvAdj : v ∈ (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList := by
      simpa using huv.2
    have hne := hedges u huRange v hvAdj
    simpa using hne

theorem coloringOK_complete
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : Array Bool)
    (hwf : g.well_formed)
    (hvalid : g.is_valid_coloring colors) :
    coloringOK g colors.toList = true := by
  rw [coloringOK_eq_true_iff]
  constructor
  · simpa using hvalid.1
  · intro u huRange v hvAdj
    have huGraph : u < g.adj.size := by
      simpa [BipartiteGraph.size] using List.mem_range.mp huRange
    have hvEdge : v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := by
      simpa using hvAdj
    have huColors : u < colors.size := by
      rw [hvalid.1]
      exact huGraph
    have hvGraph : v < g.adj.size :=
      hwf u huGraph v hvEdge
    have hvColors : v < colors.size := by
      rw [hvalid.1]
      exact hvGraph
    have hne :=
      hvalid.2 u v ⟨huGraph, hvEdge⟩ huColors hvColors
    simpa using hne
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem check_bipartite_postcond_satisfied (graph : BipartiteGraph)
    (h_precond : check_bipartite_precond graph) :
    check_bipartite_postcond graph (check_bipartite graph h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  unfold check_bipartite
  cases hsearch :
      searchColorings graph (allColorings graph.size) with
  | none =>
      simp only [check_bipartite_postcond]
      intro hbipartite
      rcases hbipartite with ⟨colors, hvalid⟩
      have hlength : colors.toList.length = graph.size := by
        simpa using hvalid.1
      have hmem : colors.toList ∈ allColorings graph.size :=
        (mem_allColorings_iff colors.toList graph.size).2 hlength
      have hfalse : coloringOK graph colors.toList = false :=
        (searchColorings_none_iff
          graph (allColorings graph.size)).1 hsearch colors.toList hmem
      have htrue : coloringOK graph colors.toList = true :=
        coloringOK_complete graph colors h_precond hvalid
      exact (by simpa [htrue] using hfalse)
  | some colors =>
      simp only [check_bipartite_postcond]
      apply coloringOK_sound
      exact searchColorings_some_ok
        graph colors (allColorings graph.size) hsearch
  -- !benchmark @end proof

  colors.size = g.size ∧

    u < colors.size → v < colors.size → colors.getD u false ≠ colors.getD v false

    (g : BipartiteGraph) (c : List Bool) (cs : List (List Bool))
    (h : searchColorings g cs = some c) :
    coloringOK g c = true := by
  induction cs with
  | nil =>
      simp [searchColorings] at h
  | cons a cs ih =>
      cases ha : coloringOK g a with
      | false =>
          simp [searchColorings, ha] at h
          exact ih h
      | true =>
          simp [searchColorings, ha] at h

theorem searchColorings_none_iff
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (cs : List (List Bool)) :
    searchColorings g cs = none ↔
      ∀ c, c ∈ cs → coloringOK g c = false := by
  induction cs with
  | nil =>
      simp [searchColorings]
  | cons a cs ih =>
      cases ha : coloringOK g a <;>

theorem coloringOK_sound
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : List Bool)
    (h : coloringOK g colors = true) :
    g.is_valid_coloring colors.toArray := by
  rw [coloringOK_eq_true_iff] at h
  rcases h with ⟨hsize, hedges⟩
  constructor
  · simpa [BipartiteGraph.size] using hsize
  · intro u v huv _hu _hv
    have huRange : u ∈ List.range g.size := by
      exact List.mem_range.mpr huv.1
    have hvAdj : v ∈ (g.adj.getD u #[]).toList := by
      simpa using huv.2
    have hne := hedges u huRange v hvAdj
    simpa using hne

theorem coloringOK_complete
    (g : BipartiteGraph) (colors : Array Bool)
    (hwf : g.well_formed)
    (hvalid : g.is_valid_coloring colors) :
    coloringOK g colors.toList = true := by
  rw [coloringOK_eq_true_iff]
  constructor
  · simpa using hvalid.1
  · intro u huRange v hvAdj
    have huGraph : u < g.adj.size := by
      simpa [BipartiteGraph.size] using List.mem_range.mp huRange
    have hvEdge : v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := by
      simpa using hvAdj
    have huColors : u < colors.size := by
      rw [hvalid.1]
      exact huGraph
    have hvGraph : v < g.adj.size :=
      hwf u huGraph v hvEdge
    have hvColors : v < colors.size := by
      rw [hvalid.1]
      exact hvGraph
    have hne :=
      hvalid.2 u v ⟨huGraph, hvEdge⟩ huColors hvColors
    simpa using hne

analysis:
The student does not implement the required algorithm in the natural language sense.

What the problem asks for:
- Implement an algorithm to check bipartiteness by attempting a 2-coloring of the graph.
- If `Some(colors)` is returned, prove the coloring is valid.
- If `None` is returned, prove no valid 2-coloring exists.
- Handle disconnected graphs correctly.
- The description strongly suggests a graph-coloring/search procedure over connected components, with the hard part being proving that a discovered coloring conflict implies non-bipartiteness.

What the student actually implements:
- `allColorings : Nat → List (List Bool)` enumerates every boolean assignment of length `n`.
- `searchColorings` linearly searches through all possible colorings.
- `check_bipartite` simply searches over all `2^n` colorings and returns the first valid one.

So this is a brute-force exhaustive search over all colorings, not the intended bipartite-checking algorithm based on propagating colors through the graph/components (e.g. BFS/DFS 2-coloring). It does satisfy input-output behavior, but the task explicitly asks for implementing the bipartite checking algorithm, and mentions specific proof obligations about forced colors/conflicts in a component. The student's solution avoids that algorithmic challenge entirely by reducing non-bipartiteness to “no coloring in the finite enumeration works.”

About disconnected graphs:
- Their brute-force method does handle disconnected graphs globally, since it checks all assignments. So this part is semantically fine.
- However, this does not rescue the mismatch in required implementation approach.

About cheating/tricks:
- I do not see `sorry`, `admit`, empty bodies, or reliance on an external pre-verified bipartite checker.
- The student did write an actual implementation and supporting proofs.
- So this is not compiler-trick cheating.

But the core issue remains:
- The natural language description requires implementing the bipartite-checking/2-coloring algorithm, while the student instead uses exhaustive enumeration of all colorings.
- This is analogous to implementing bubble sort when quicksort was required: functionally correct, but not the required algorithmic approach.

Therefore the answer should be rejected on semantic grounds.
